title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Three leaders, one table, no Ukraine
preheader: The White House says Trump will discuss Iran and nuclear arms, but not Russia's war.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Saturday, November 14, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 3 updates on stories you're following and 4 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way summit in China
stories.why_important: The White House says the three leaders will meet next week in Shenzhen on APEC's sidelines. Trump plans to discuss nuclear arms and Iran, but not Russia's war in Ukraine.
stories.what_overlooked: The meeting is still not firmly scheduled, and the White House has not said whether Putin and Xi agreed to Trump's agenda.
stories.prediction: A confirmed joint statement from the three governments would show the summit is more than a photo op.

stories.story_title: Europe names negotiators for Ukraine peace talks
stories.why_important: The EU, Germany, France, the UK, Italy and Poland will send national security advisers to represent Europe in any Russia-Ukraine talks. The move aims to give Europe a unified voice alongside US-led negotiations.
stories.what_overlooked: Ukraine has said it wants European backup, but the group has no power to negotiate without US and Russian agreement.
stories.prediction: The first meeting of these advisers will reveal whether Europe can speak with one voice.

stories.story_title: Turkey and Qatar sign mutual defense pact
stories.why_important: Turkey and Qatar agreed to a unified response to any attack on either country. The pact deepens ties between two regional allies and follows a similar Turkey-Pakistan-Saudi agreement in August.
stories.what_overlooked: The text does not say whether either country would send troops if the other is attacked.
stories.prediction: Details of joint exercises or troop deployments would show whether the pact is operational.

quick_hits.text: US flights resumed after a four-hour nationwide ground stop caused by communications failure, officials said, ruling out a cyberattack.
The UK led 53 countries and organizations in urging Israel's incoming government to allow rapid, unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza.
Germany's parliament granted police and intelligence services sweeping new powers after drone sightings and cyberattacks raised security concerns.
Russian strikes killed three people in Ukraine and injured 50 in Zaporizhzhia, including eight children, local officials said.

developing.text: US forces responded to suspected drone activity over RAF Lakenheath in Britain, the Ministry of Defence said, and the situation is now resolved.
Chinese officials called Jensen Huang's swift downfall a political hit, Nikkei Asia reported, after the Nvidia chief resigned over affairs and a spy link.
Pope Leo XIV drew an estimated 1 million people along his motorcade route in Peru, the Vatican said, during a 12-day South America tour.
